$comment: Controlled terminology (AGENTS.md Sections 15, 64, 65). Each entry maps a normalized term to the body-model structures it is ASSOCIATED with (visualizationType: association, never disease). Structure ids are body-model structure or organ-group ids (public/anatomy/body/structures.json). Synonyms are matched case-insensitively after removing punctuation and spaces. Sources: docs/MEDICAL_SOURCES.md. Each term has a display group (groups). Structure ids 'layer:arteries', 'layer:veins' and 'layer:skeleton' stand for a whole layer: used for tests measured in blood (shown on the vessels, never as a problem in a vessel) or stored in bone. Terms with no associatedStructures are recognized tests that are not linked to one organ (Section 89) or whose organ is not in the model; they are listed under their group and never highlighted.

terms.mappingReason: Creatinine is filtered from the blood by the kidneys, so it is commonly used as a kidney-associated marker.
eGFR estimates how much blood the kidneys filter each minute.
ALT is an enzyme found mainly in the liver, so it is commonly used as a liver-associated marker.
Urea nitrogen is a waste product that the kidneys remove from the blood, so BUN is commonly used as a kidney-associated marker.
Urea is a waste product that the kidneys remove from the blood, so it is commonly used as a kidney-associated marker.
AST is an enzyme found mainly in the liver (and also in the heart and muscles), so it is commonly used as a liver-associated marker.
GGT is an enzyme found mainly in the liver, so it is commonly used as a liver-associated marker.
Bilirubin is removed from the blood by the liver, so it is commonly used as a liver-associated marker.
Direct bilirubin is bilirubin already processed by the liver, so it is commonly used as a liver-associated marker.
Indirect bilirubin is bilirubin not yet processed by the liver; it is reported as part of liver-associated bilirubin testing.
Most lipase in the blood is made by the pancreas, so it is commonly used as a pancreas-associated marker.
Troponin is a protein found in heart muscle cells, so it is used as a heart-associated marker.
Troponin is a protein found in heart muscle cells, so it is used as a heart-associated marker.
Albumin is a protein made by the liver, so it is commonly used as a liver-associated marker.
ALP is an enzyme found mainly in the liver and the bones, so both are shown.

CK-MB is the form of creatine kinase found mainly in heart muscle, so it is used as a heart-associated marker.

The lungs take oxygen into the blood; this shows how much oxygen the blood is carrying, so the lungs are shown.
Respiratory rate is the number of breaths per minute, so the lungs are shown.
Peak flow measures how fast air can be blown out of the lungs, so the lungs are shown.
PaO2 reflects how well the lungs move oxygen into the blood, so the lungs are shown.
PaCO2 reflects how well the lungs remove carbon dioxide from the blood, so the lungs are shown.
Both the lungs and the kidneys help keep the blood's acid balance (pH), so both are shown.
Cortisol is a hormone made by the adrenal glands, which sit above the kidneys.
PTH is made by the parathyroid glands in the neck. They are not part of the current 3D model, so nothing is highlighted.
LH is a hormone made by the pituitary gland at the base of the brain.
FSH is a hormone made by the pituitary gland at the base of the brain.
Prolactin is a hormone made by the pituitary gland at the base of the brain.
Testosterone is made mainly by the testicles in men, and in small amounts by the ovaries and adrenal glands. Because the source depends on sex, nothing is highlighted.
SHBG is a protein made mostly in the liver that carries sex hormones in the blood, so the liver is shown.
